text:
The Ads Agent did not report, so I pulled this myself directly from live Google Ads data (account 2915572948), scoped to the two net-new campaigns the Ads Agent built: PLL-Search-Samples-2026 and PLL-Search-ContractMfg-2026 (Sam's legacy campaigns — Initial, New-Sales-Ad, Sales Campaign PLL — are excluded from every figure below). Note: I could not independently verify the exact seven-ad roster within these campaigns (ad-level tool access was not available this run), so treat the ad count as unverified — these figures are at the campaign level, not individually confirmed per ad.

Trailing 7 days (2026-07-26 to 2026-08-01): spend $201.88, impressions 624, clicks 87, CTR 13.94%, avg CPC $2.32. Breakdown — Samples: spend $48.93, impr 242, clicks 33, CTR 13.64%, avg CPC $1.48. ContractMfg: spend $152.95, impr 382, clicks 54, CTR 14.14%, avg CPC $2.83.

Prior 7 days (2026-07-19 to 2026-07-25): spend $128.52, impressions 415, clicks 68, CTR 16.39%, avg CPC $1.89. Breakdown — Samples: spend $47.47, impr 133, clicks 32, CTR 24.06%, avg CPC $1.48. ContractMfg: spend $81.05, impr 282, clicks 36, CTR 12.77%, avg CPC $2.25.

What changed: total spend rose $73.36 (+57.1%) week over week, driven almost entirely by ContractMfg, whose spend rose $71.90 (+88.7%) on 50% more clicks but also a higher avg CPC ($2.25 to $2.83). Samples spend was flat (+$1.46) but its CTR fell from 24.06% to 13.64% on roughly double the impressions — same clicks, more impressions, i.e. reach grew faster than engagement.

Lead/booked-call attribution: NOT YET MEASURABLE via this pull — no UTM/GCLID or conversion-action evidence was queried or found in this data source, so I cannot state how many of these clicks produced leads or booked calls.

Recommendation: investigate why ContractMfg's avg CPC climbed toward $2.83-$4.13/day range late in the current window (see 7/28, 7/30, 7/31, 8/1 daily CPCs) — check for auction pressure or a keyword-match drift before letting spend keep climbing, and confirm current-window total ($201.88) against the $210/week hard cap before any further spend this week.
spoken_text: Sam, here's the bottom line. The Ads Agent didn't report on this one, so I pulled the numbers myself, straight from Google Ads, for just its two net new campaigns. Over the last seven days those two campaigns spent about two hundred two dollars, on eighty seven clicks and healthy click through rates in the low teens percent. Compared with the seven days before that, spend jumped about fifty seven percent, and that increase came almost entirely from the contract manufacturing campaign, where the average cost per click also crept up. The sample campaign held spend flat but its click through rate cooled off some. I can't yet tell you how many leads or booked calls came out of this, since we don't have ad tracking wired up to confirm that. My read is the cost per click rise on contract manufacturing is worth a look before letting it keep climbing, especially since we're bumping up near the weekly budget cap. I'd recommend checking that campaign's recent auction activity and keyword matching this week before spending more.
